_comment: Numbers that scripts enforce. Prose and reasons live in style/STYLE_GUIDE.md. Change a value here and every shot follows.

safe_area._comment: Fractions of the frame covered by the Shorts UI. Faces, clues and key action stay inside what is left.

look._comment: The approved look (docs/LOOK_AUDIT_PHASE1.md section 10). white_balance_k 6500 = off; a light rig may set its own per time of day.

checks._comment: Read by stagekit/review.py for the look checks on final-quality stills (review/<shot>/look/). Calibrated on the training-room study: the film's light must fail, the approved picture must pass. Face means are 0-1; luma tenths and chroma are 0-255; warmth is mean V minus mean U.

captions._comment: One short caption at a time, centred on the frame, on one fixed line. Measured on the reference Shorts: 1 word 75%, 2 words 22%, 3 words 3%; centred at x=0.50; line at 0.70-0.72 of the height; each caption appears about 0.1 s before its word and stays until the next one.

finish._comment: Applied once in Remotion over the whole film so every shot gets the same finish.

shots.note: A shot is one staged take in one set and one time of day (a render unit). Most Shorts need 2-5. The viewer sees them through views.

views._comment: A view is one camera framing inside a shot. per_short is the validator's sanity range (tools/plan.py, tools/qa.py warn outside it), not the aim: the four reference Shorts hold 22-33 framings per minute (reference_framings_per_minute, read by nobody, it is the target the director plans to). The upper bound is the top of the reference pace (33), so a plan at reference pace is not warned; a plan far below it is the one to question.

sets._comment: Read by stagekit/audit.py (tools/blender/set_preview.py). A wide view of a finished set must clear every minimum; the audit blocks on any miss.

camera._comment: Read by stagekit/camera.py (drift) and stagekit/campath.py (limits). Measured on four reference Shorts: the camera moves 60-80% of screen time, held views still drift 2-5%. A whip (0.25-0.5 s) is exempt from the speed limits. Exceeding a limit warns; exceeding it by block_factor blocks.

cast._comment: How the cast is staged. The cast is solid 3D (any angle, back views and walking away are fine): max_camera_tilt_deg is the pitch past which review.py warns steep_angle with characters in frame. depth_squash is for the old flat 2D pack only.

physical._comment: Read by stagekit/physical.py (the measured physical checks: contact, passage, grip, carry, reach). Values come from the two prototype reports (output/experiments/exp_a_collision, exp_b_interaction). Depths in cm, distances in m, angles in degrees. A fault outside the camera's view at its worst on-screen frame is a warning.
